past_medical_history: Osteoarthritis bilateral knees (total knee replacement left 2 years ago)
family_history: No family history of dementia or neurological disease

patient.chief_complaint: Gait instability, 'slowness' of thought, and urinary urgency for 14 months
patient.history_present_illness: A 71-year-old right-handed retired nurse with hypertension, hyperlipidemia, and history of left knee replacement was admitted from the neurology outpatient clinic for inpatient tap trial evaluation after 14 months of progressive triad symptoms. The patient, a former nurse who is knowledgeable about her own health, first noticed gait changes approximately 14 months ago — she describes her feet as feeling 'like they are stuck to the floor' and she began using a walker after two near-falls in the home. She notes that her gait instability is disproportionate to the bilateral knee pain — she has had worsening bilateral knee osteoarthritis but her orthopedic surgeon told her that her gait pattern is 'not just the arthritis.' Over approximately the same period she has developed urinary urgency that occasionally results in urge incontinence before reaching the bathroom. She wears pads 'just in case.' Her daughter has noted she is more 'vague' and 'slow to respond' in conversations over the past 8 months — she repeats herself more and takes longer to find words than previously. She scored 21/30 on MoCA at the outpatient appointment (loses on attention, trail-making, and recall). Brain MRI obtained outpatient showed 'communicating hydrocephalus with moderate white matter disease.' Evans index measured at 0.32 on outpatient review. Callosal angle was measured at 96 degrees on coronal imaging — equivocal (borderline value is <90 degrees for NPH). Admission is for high-volume tap trial.

neurological_exam.mental_status: Alert, fully oriented. Speech mildly slowed but fluent. Word-finding mildly impaired. MoCA 21/30 — loses 4 points on attention and working memory, 3 on recall, 1 on visuospatial. Clock drawing mildly impaired (misplaced hands). No apraxia.
neurological_exam.cranial_nerves: Pupils equal, 3mm, reactive. EOMs full. Facial sensation intact. Tongue midline.
neurological_exam.motor: Mild bilateral lower extremity stiffness — increased tone at ankles. Upper extremity tone normal. Strength 5/5 throughout. No tremor.
neurological_exam.sensory: Vibration mildly reduced at ankles. Joint position sense intact at toes.
neurological_exam.reflexes: 2+ biceps, brachioradialis. 2+ patellar bilaterally. Achilles 1+. Plantar flexor bilaterally.
neurological_exam.coordination: Finger-nose intact. Heel-shin mildly awkward bilaterally.
neurological_exam.gait: Wide-based, short-stepped gait. Reduced foot clearance. Takes 4-5 steps to initiate. Turns en bloc requiring 5-6 steps. Unable to perform tandem gait. Uses walker. TUG 28 seconds (with walker). 10-meter walk 22 seconds.
neurological_exam.additional: No resting tremor. No cogwheel rigidity. Pull test: one step backward but recovers without falling (mildly impaired postural reflexes).

signal_characteristics.description: Moderately enlarged lateral ventricles, Evans index 0.32
Moderate bilateral periventricular and subcortical FLAIR/T2 hyperintensity
Callosal angle 96 degrees on coronal T1
Mild tightening of high convexity sulci

mri.impression: 1. Moderate ventriculomegaly; Evans index 0.32. Callosal angle 96 degrees on coronal T1. Mild tightening of high-convexity sulci. 2. Moderate bilateral periventricular and subcortical FLAIR/T2 white matter hyperintensity. Clinical correlation recommended.

csf.interpretation: Opening pressure: 14 cmH2O. WBC: 2 cells/mcL (N/A PMN/N/A lymph). Protein: 44 mg/dL. Glucose: 64 mg/dL (ratio 0.68). cytology: No malignant cells. beta_amyloid_42: 824 pg/mL (normal; reference >650). total_tau: 188 pg/mL (normal; reference <300). phospho_tau: 28 pg/mL (normal; reference <61).

specialized_test.test_type: High-volume tap trial (40 mL) with gait analysis and cognitive testing

findings.gait_description: Post-tap: improved step length, less freezing at initiation, improved foot clearance, still wide-based

specialized_test.impression: High-volume tap trial (40 mL): TUG improved from 28 seconds pre-tap to 21.5 seconds at 24 hours (23% improvement). 10-meter walk improved from 22 to 17 seconds at 24 hours (23% improvement). MoCA improved 1 point at 24 hours. Post-tap gait description: improved step length, reduced freezing at initiation, improved foot clearance; remains wide-based. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.impression: Phase-contrast MRI (aqueductal CSF flow): peak velocity 19.5 cm/s (reference <18 cm/s); net stroke volume 52 mcL/cycle (reference <42 mcL/cycle). Mildly hyperdynamic aqueductal CSF pulsatility identified. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.day_1_drainage: 148 mL; TUG improved from 28 to 20 sec (29%)

findings.cognitive: MoCA improved from 21 to 23/30 at end of drainage trial

output.impression: Extended lumbar drainage (446 mL over 72 hours): progressive gait improvement to 33% TUG reduction at day 3 (from 28 seconds baseline to 18.8 seconds). MoCA improved 2 points over the drainage period. No adverse events. Clinical correlation recommended.

quantitative_data.overall_pattern: Frontal-subcortical cognitive dysfunction consistent with NPH and/or vascular white matter disease

output.impression: Neuropsychological evaluation demonstrates a frontal-subcortical pattern of cognitive dysfunction: executive function moderately impaired, processing speed moderately-severely impaired, episodic memory mildly-moderately impaired, language with mild word-finding difficulty only. Profile consistent with predominant frontal-subcortical cognitive dysfunction. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.finding: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity — involuntary contractions at 160 mL fill

output.impression: Neurogenic detrusor overactivity identified: involuntary detrusor contractions at 160 mL fill. First sensation of filling reduced at 80 mL. Reduced bladder capacity 240 mL (reference 400–500 mL). No urodynamic evidence of outlet obstruction. Clinical correlation recommended.

findings.result: Negative amyloid PET — CL score 12 (well below threshold of 24.4)

output.impression: Negative — sparse-to-no amyloid neuritic plaque density. CL score 12, below the amyloid positivity threshold. Clinical correlation recommended.

output.proposed: Perioperative management for VP shunt: cefazolin prophylaxis, hold sertraline considerations
interactions: Sertraline: SSRI discontinuation syndrome if stopped abruptly; taper rather than abrupt cessation if necessary
warnings: Continue sertraline perioperatively — abrupt cessation risks serotonin discontinuation syndrome and depression relapse
Amlodipine: continue perioperatively; discuss with anesthesia

background.pdr: 9-10 Hz posterior dominant rhythm, symmetric and reactive
background.sleep_features: normal vertex waves and sleep spindles

eeg.impression: Normal awake and drowsy EEG. No epileptiform discharges and no focal slowing.

findings: Normal sinus rhythm. Normal axis and intervals. No acute ST-T changes.
Grade I (mild) diastolic dysfunction, age-appropriate. No intracardiac thrombus or vegetation. No pericardial effusion.
echo.impression: Structurally near-normal heart with a benign incidental finding.

findings: No sustained arrhythmia. No pauses greater than 2 seconds. No AV block.

general.summary: No directly applicable, high-quality evidence was retrieved for this query. Recommend correlating with current society guidelines.

differential.key_features: Moderate white matter disease, hypertension, hyperlipidemia — but Evans index 0.32, positive tap trial, neurogenic detrusor overactivity support NPH as primary diagnosis; vascular disease likely co-contributor
Cognitive decline — but MoCA pattern is frontal-subcortical, CSF biomarkers normal, amyloid PET negative — Alzheimer's co-pathology not supported
Gait disorder — but no tremor, no rigidity, no asymmetry, ventriculomegaly on imaging
Bilateral knee OA with knee replacement — but magnetic gait is disproportionate to knee findings per orthopedics

optimal_actions.action: Review brain MRI — Evans index, callosal angle, white matter disease, tight sulci
optimal_actions.expected_finding: Evans 0.32, equivocal callosal angle 96 degrees, moderate WMH

optimal_actions.action: Comprehensive metabolic labs — exclude reversible causes
High-volume tap trial with formal gait assessment
Extended 72h lumbar drainage trial given equivocal tap result

critical_actions: Tap trial with formal TUG and 10-meter walk test before and after is mandatory
Extended lumbar drainage trial appropriate when single tap trial is equivocal
Normal CSF biomarkers and negative amyloid PET strengthen VP shunt indication
Do not attribute entire syndrome to knee osteoarthritis — gait pattern is magnetic gait not orthopedic gait
contraindicated_actions: Attributing gait entirely to knee osteoarthritis without tap trial
VP shunting without any tap trial or drainage trial in borderline imaging case
key_reasoning_points: Equivocal callosal angle (96 degrees, just above the 90-degree criterion) adds to moderate difficulty
Extended lumbar drainage trial is the appropriate next step when single tap trial is equivocal-positive — it provides stronger prediction of shunt response
Negative amyloid PET provides favorable prognostic information for shunt response
Significant vascular white matter disease may contribute independently to symptoms but does not preclude NPH diagnosis

red_herrings.data_point: Left knee replacement 2 years ago with ongoing bilateral knee osteoarthritis
red_herrings.intended_effect: Gait disorder attributed to orthopedic causes, delaying NPH evaluation
red_herrings.correct_interpretation: Orthopedic surgeon noted gait pattern atypical for knee disease; magnetic gait with wide base and reduced foot clearance is not the typical antalgic or Trendelenburg gait of knee pathology

metadata.difficulty_variant_description: Moderate NPH — equivocal callosal angle (96 degrees), moderate WMH, equivocal-positive tap trial (23%); extended drainage trial strengthens diagnosis.
